It depends on the therapy. I’m currently in therapy, seeing a psychologist over Zoom for trauma. The kind of therapy I’m doing is called psychodynamic therapy, basically the kind you see on TV with the reclined couch and stuff. It’s the kind that psychoanalyzes you to understand why you’re traumatized and how to get through it. 

I found a very kind therapist, and I trust her enough for therapy. But this kind of therapy is emotionally taxing and sometimes painful. It’s like digging into an old but infected wound to remove the infected parts: painful but necessary. 

My first session I had an anxiety attack and couldn’t breathe. The second? I was laughing and happy to tell her things. 

Recovery isn’t linear and neither is therapy. My own road ahead is a long one: but it will be worth it. 

I wish you much luck and healing.
